title: Names hold values

blocks.md:
## A name is a sticky note

A name is a sticky note you press onto a value after you finish a calculation. The note does not do the math. It only remembers the result so you can use that result again without typing the work twice. `total = 3 + 4` computes the sum, then sticks `7` on the name `total`. `print(total)` shows whatever that name holds right now.

This bites when you print a hardcoded `7` and skip the name. The screen looks correct once, but nothing is storing the answer. Change the sum later and the printed digit stays stale, because you never attached a name to the result.

```python
total = 3 + 4
print(total)
```

A common mistake is treating `print` as the storage. Printing a literal skips the sticky-note idea entirely. The exercise asks you to compute `3 + 4` into the name `total`, then print that name so the output is `7` because of the stored value, not because you typed the digit yourself.

hintLadder.md: Compute 3 + 4 into a name, then print the name.
The last line should print a name, not a hardcoded 7 only.
